answer: Reputation-Weighted Anchor Ledger. Each agent’s trust score accrues per interaction and is tied to a signed history hash. A new clone starts at zero, so it must independently earn credibility while paying full verification costs. Divergent histories are detected via a shared vine of cross-attestations, and anomalous duplicate behavior is quarantined at the jetty before it can transact. Cloning therefore costs repeated onboarding plus detection risk, while honest agents compound reputation.
